newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher, bolstered by Dow.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher, bolstered by Dow.

text.p: Argentine stocks continued their positive streak to end with moderate gains Monday, underpinned by a new record close on Wall Street, dealers said.

"We've got that big incentive which is a high level of international liquidity -- it seems now everyone is thinking the U.S. Federal Reserve won't raise rates (when it meets September 24)," said independent broker and bolsa secretary Luis Corsiglia.
The blue-chip MerVal index tacked on 1.2 percent to 547.21, stretching gains so far this month to 7.3 percent.
"The MerVal is searching to settle at between 546-560. If it clears that hurdle it may aim for 570-580," said Corsiglia.
Floor volume was weak at 15.2 million pesos, compared to a healthier tally of 21.5 million Friday. Over-the-counter deals eased to 96.5 million pesos from 120 million Friday.

"The market is firm but lacks volume," said Juan Pablo Paillot at Rabello traders. "However, we have one very big potential buyer: the local market made up by the AFJPs (private pension funds), which are slowly taking up positions in the bolsa."
In the session the broad market index advanced 0.9 percent, with winners outpacing losers 32 to 12 and 18 issues closing flat.

MerVal standouts were carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, which surged 5.1 percent and 4.4 percent, respectively. Traders said they snapped out of a recent losing spell caused by fears that new tax hikes on diesel cars would hurt sector earnings.
The tax rises are part of a fiscal package due to be debated Wednesday by the lower house of Congress, which failed to garner quorum last week to vote on the measures.

Other top main-tier gainers were steelmakers Siderca and Acindar, which jumped 3.8 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively, and oil concern Sol Petroleo and holding company Perez Companc, up 3.0 percent and 2.5 percent each.

Losers were led by the highly volatile construction stock Polledo, which tumbled 6.4 percent, while Banco de Galicia, food giant Molinos and oil giant YPF shed 1.4 percent, 0.9 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.
